# Premise falsified — the 1M-file ceiling this task was filed on has been resolved; parking at `on_hold`

Posted by the `/issue 2286` session (2026-08-22). #2286, **#2287** and #2300 are
three independent filings of the SAME condition on 2026-08-14 (from #2254, #2225
and #2094 respectively). The condition is gone. This note records the evidence so
no further session re-derives it; the systemic fix for the duplication itself is
**#2390**.

## This task's premise

> "Current count ≈ 999,867; remaining headroom ≈ 133 files FLEET-WIDE."

**Measured 2026-08-19 (#2321, three independent reads agreeing): 454,804 /
1,000,000 — 545,196 slots free.** Behavioral confirmation: a scan of every
`tasks/*/*/events.jsonl` for the Hub's verbatim file-count rejection text with
`ts >= 2026-08-17` returns **zero hits**, across five days of heavy fleet
uploading.

## Scope-item-by-scope-item coverage

1. **"Measure + report per-top-level-prefix file counts … identify the dominant
   consumers"** — DONE. #2321 and #2332 both produced the same measured top-10
   inventory (610,356 files across the ten largest prefixes), prefix-scoped as
   this task prescribed.
2. **"Cleanup candidates (PROPOSE ONLY — HF deletions are USER-ONLY)"** — DONE and
   then executed under explicit user authorization: #2332 repacked and reclaimed
   **492,786 slots** (938,366 → 445,580 files), every prefix with
   `kept_stale=0, kept_new=0`, with the packed-path reader
   (`src/explore_persona_space/orchestrate/packed_prefix.py`) landed on
   `origin/main` so consumers still resolve the original paths. The
   USER-ONLY property was honoured throughout: #2321's parallel driver refused
   off-premise at its own cap probe with zero deletions rather than proceeding.
3. **"Standing policy: data-repo file-count clause — (a) headroom probe,
   (b) overflow routing for file-count, (c) guidance to PACK high-count
   uploads"** — DONE by #2304 (`.claude/rules/upload-policy.md` +77 lines,
   `origin/main`): (a) the WARN-only preflight `check_hf_filecount_sentinel`
   (`preflight.py:1876`, structurally incapable of failing a launch — it only
   ever calls `report.add_warning`); (b) file-count overflow routing to
   `superkaiba1/explore-persona-space-overflow` with the `OVERFLOW_POINTER`
   breadcrumb and a distinguishable degraded reason when the canonical repo is
   too full to accept even the pointer; (c) the packing/sharding clauses
   (<9 MB `.shardNN.jsonl`, never gzip; manifest-first consumer resolution,
   #2119; `hub.stage_sharded_text`), plus `upload_dir_sharded` (#1824)
   collapsing small-file stores into one `upload_folder` commit.
4. **"Mechanical arm: wire the file-count rejection into hub.py as a typed,
   non-retryable error"** — SUBSTANTIALLY done, with one possible sliver.
   `_is_file_count_limit_error` (deliberately digit-free and exception-class
   agnostic — the message is the contract) now gates the shared
   `_filecount_overflow_retry` helper, called from BOTH `_upload` and
   `_upload_folder_filtered` on `origin/main` (`hub.py:1451` admits
   `repo_type in ("model", "dataset")`). So the rejection is recognised and
   ROUTED rather than surfacing as a generic `BadRequestError` after retries.
   What this task additionally asked for and #2304 did not add verbatim is a
   distinct *typed exception class* raised when routing itself is unavailable
   (e.g. the kill switch `EPM_HF_FILECOUNT_FALLBACK=0`, or the overflow repo
   also refusing). That residue is small, no longer urgent, and is the only
   reason this task is parked rather than proposed for archival.

urgent premise is dead, but scope item 4's typed-exception residue is a real (if
minor) judgement call that belongs to Thomas, not to an autonomous session.
